title: ADscan attack paths snapshot v1
description: domains/<domain>/attack_paths_snapshot.json: the attack paths the engine computed for one domain at the end of a scan, each with its steps and the status ADscan proved for it. Written by one writer (persist_attack_path_snapshot in adscan_internal/cli/attack_path_execution.py). Version marker: schema_version, '1.<minor>'. Declared objects may gain fields within a major; do not reject unknown keys. Step details, knowledge and remediability are opaque.

scope.$comment: Which sources the search started from (domain, owned, principal, ...).

id.$comment: Listing-local token, not stable across runs. Use path_id to refer to a route.

path_id.$comment: Since 1.1. The path id: the ordered-route fingerprint, stable across runs. The web platform keys its attack-path records on it, the report prints its first 12 characters, and adscan recheck --path takes any unambiguous prefix of 8 or more.

status.$comment: theoretical, attempted, partial, exploited, blocked, closed_by_configuration, unsupported (open vocabulary). Only exploited means every step was executed.

path_state.$comment: Lifecycle state of a proven path (domain_compromised, ...); null when not proven.

compromise_class.$comment: domain_breaker, tier0_control, tier0_foothold, privileged_escalator, compromise_enabler, unauthenticated_principal or none.

node_kinds.$comment: Directory object class per node, parallel to nodes.

status.$comment: success, attempted, blocked, theoretical, structural, discovered, closed_by_configuration, unsupported (open vocabulary).
